purpose: Align historical static and browser contracts with the already-canonical Surface Standard runtime without weakening assertions or changing backend/runtime authority.

saturationImpact.reason: This slice changes evidence consumers only; it introduces no new runtime layout, lexical, authority or standards primitive.

invariants.name: semantic-token-declaration
invariants.rule: Historical design-system assurance must validate the declared CSS custom-property syntax --ds-ease:, not the invalid literal --ds-ease;.

invariants.name: progressive-settings-sequencing
invariants.rule: The browser journey must fill organization fields while the organization disclosure is open, then open the provider disclosure and fill provider fields.

invariants.name: progressive-job-sequencing
invariants.rule: The browser journey must open the criteria and schedule job groups before interacting with controls moved into those groups.

invariants.name: canonical-terminal-vocabulary
invariants.rule: Historical browser assertions must consume the terminal labels Accetta nel catalogo, Accettata nel catalogo and Scarica evidenza.

invariants.name: no-runtime-bypass
invariants.rule: Alignment must not force hidden controls, disable single-open behavior, modify server authority, or reintroduce legacy labels in production code.

invariants.name: same-head-evidence
invariants.rule: Historical-contract assurance, Surface Standard assurance, server-backed browser and general CI must execute against the same PR head before the slice is considered mature.

observedFailures.observation: enterprise-2-design-system-check expected --ds-ease; while the runtime declares --ds-ease:cubic-bezier(...).
browser-product-check opened provider after organization and then attempted to fill organizationName after single-open behavior had hidden that section.

preventiveAlignments.reason: authorities and sourceHints are now owned by closed criteria/schedule groups and must be opened before interaction.
source acceptance/status and evidence-download assertions must use the canonical terminal vocabulary already rendered by the runtime.

acceptance: The semantic-token historical check passes without changing the design-system CSS token declaration.
The product browser journey completes settings configuration through the single-open progressive disclosure contract.
The product browser journey completes job configuration by explicitly opening each required disclosure owner.
Source decision and event evidence assertions use canonical terminal labels.
No production UI, API, permission, capability or backend authority code is changed by this alignment slice.
Surface Standard assurance and its server-backed browser remain green on the final slice head.
General CI is re-evaluated on the final slice head; any newly exposed failure becomes the next falsifiable finding rather than being masked.
claimBoundary: This model demonstrates alignment of historical evidence consumers with the declared runtime contract. It does not establish universal regression freedom, accessibility conformance, legal compliance, certification or production readiness.
